bibliographic.title: Preserving attribution and accountability in AI-scale systems
bibliographic.citation_apa: Gahl, F. C. (2026). Preserving attribution and accountability in AI-scale systems. Discover Artificial Intelligence, 6, 564. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-026-01415-9

methodology.study_design: conceptual paper introducing BlockClaim provenance framework with literature-informed analysis of attribution failure modes
methodology.technology_context: AI-mediated information systems; AI-scale systems involving ingestion, transformation, and recombination of human-produced material; provenance and attribution infrastructure

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article offers a strong conceptual contribution on attribution, accountability, traceability, and governance enablers in AI-scale systems, but the provided text contains no explicit treatment of conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, or LLM-specific operational governance in regulated deployments. It is better suited as foundational/contextual evidence for accountability infrastructure than as central evidence for conversational LLM governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Metadata title extraction is corrupted; only partial full text was supplied; conversational-AI and LLM-specific fit must be verified across the complete manuscript.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based on abstract, introduction, and scattered section excerpts only. The study is explicitly conceptual and infrastructural rather than empirical; sampling and data-collection criteria are not applicable in the usual empirical sense.

cerqual.explanation: The argumentative structure is coherent and the objective is clearly stated, but available text shows limited empirical validation and only partial direct relevance to conversational LLM governance in regulated operational contexts.

coding.theme: Attribution and provenance as infrastructural preconditions for AI accountability
coding.subtheme: Minimal non-adjudicative provenance framework for AI-mediated claim traceability
model_layers: downstream governance and institutional evaluation layer

synthesis.main_claim: Stable attribution and temporal priority are fragile infrastructural conditions required for accountability in AI-scale systems, and BlockClaim is proposed as a minimal provenance framework to preserve claim history without adjudicating truth, ethics, or enforcement.
synthesis.contribution: Reframes AI accountability challenges as problems of preserved traceability and introduces a neutral provenance framework intended to support downstream ethical, legal, and institutional processes.
synthesis.limitations: The framework is not presented as a comprehensive governance solution and remains neutral with respect to truth, ethics, and enforcement; attribution collapse may not be adequately addressed by downstream governance alone.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational/contextual evidence on accountability, traceability, and provenance infrastructure in AI-mediated systems; not recommended as central evidence for conversational LLM governance unless fuller text shows direct conversational or LLM-operational relevance.
